pcg_graph_feasibility.artifact: LandscapeLab/Content/Scratch/PCG/PCG_ClutterSpike.uasset (64,732 bytes, saved from Python, gitignored under Content/Scratch)
pcg_graph_feasibility.what_it_proves: A real PCG graph -- SurfaceSampler(points_per_squared_meter) -> TransformPoints -> StaticMeshSpawner(PCGMeshSelectorWeighted, descriptor.static_mesh set) -- was created and SAVED entirely from the Python reflected API (add_node_of_type / add_edge / set_mesh_selector_type / PCGRuntimeGenerationRadii.radius400). PCG authoring from Python is FEASIBLE. This is the queue's core feasibility question, answered YES.
pcg_graph_feasibility.known_gaps: Edges into/out of the Input/Output nodes use pin labels the design-review flagged as non-'In'/'Out' (PCGInputOutputSettings.cpp) and AddEdge is non-raising, so those two edges may have silently no-op'd; the middle sampler->transform->spawner edges use 'Out'/'In' correctly. Runtime generation was NOT executed/scheduled this pass.

measurement.metric_intended: game-thread wall-clock of InstancedFoliageActor.add_instances (the foliage/PCG spawn stage) per 1000 instances, by class, at 3 counts. Proven idiom (place_foliage.py).
why_not_captured: This harness REAPS background commands (>120s auto-background) at turn boundaries. The measurement payload's Python CLIENT was killed twice mid-run.
The editor was launched detached (not reaped) and kept executing the payload after the client died, so the arm-result JSON printed to a dead remote-exec channel and was lost.

The big payload (up to 20,000 instances x 18 arms + per-class collect_garbage in an 18 GB editor) then held the editor's single Python thread, blocking remote-exec for ~25 min; the editor was force-killed (disk-safe: PCG graph already saved, level never saved).
A fast measurement-only payload (base 1000, no GC) was prepared to run <120s foreground, but the editor never freed to accept it.
measurement.retry_recipe_for_a_supervised_session: With an editor already loaded on /Game/Alpine8K and remote-exec responsive, run scratchpad/pcg_measure_fast.py (base 1000, no per-class GC) via ue_exec in the FOREGROUND (completes <120s, so no background reap). It reports arms[].add_ms_per_1000 by class. For GPU render cost, save the FoliageType instances into a scratch level and run an item8-class -game MRQ pass.

owed: game-thread clutter add/generation cost per 1000 by class (the fast payload above; ~minutes supervised)
steady-state GPU render cost per 1000 by class (a -game MRQ pass on a saved scratch level)
